title: Al-Wasi', the All-Encompassing
hookLine: the All-Encompassing, vast in mercy and knowledge
tomorrow: why would a wise man knock a hole in a poor man's boat?

cards: Kayla texted Amira last night: want to practice interview questions together? Same scholarship, same final round, one spot. They patched things up at senior night.

But practicing together means handing your best answers to the person you're up against. Amira left it on read for an hour, thumb hovering. Some invitations ask a heart to stretch a size bigger than it is.
Today's Name is about that kind of size.

teach.h: EAST AND WEST, AND HIS COUNTENANCE.
teach.b: Al-Wasi', the All-Encompassing, the Vast. Surah Al-Baqarah: "Unto Allah belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance. Lo! Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing."
Vast in two ways at once: in mercy, and in knowledge.
In Surah Al-A'raf, Allah says: "My mercy embraceth all things." All things. That leaves room for Kayla, and room for Amira on a petty day.
And vast doesn't mean distant: the same verse that gives God every direction says His Countenance is wherever you turn. Now hold the week up to that sky.
Al-Muqit, the Nourisher: food for the body, knowledge for the heart. Al-Hasib, who counts every returned hello, and is enough. Al-Jalil, majesty that comes paired with generous honor.
Al-Karim, giving before the ask, shy to send raised hands back empty. Ar-Raqib, watching every word, for your sake. Al-Mujib, near enough to answer.
Six Names, and Al-Wasi' holds all of them, the way a sky holds weather.
A week of food, counting, awe, gifts, words and asking, and none of it falls outside.
Here's the thought to take to a friend: if His mercy embraces all things, a human heart can stretch to fit one rival for one practice session.

how: Muslims call on Allah as al-Wasi' among the Names in du'a, and 2:115, 'whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance', is recited as a reminder that no place is outside His reach.

o: the one who rules the East and the West
the Vast, wide in mercy and in knowledge
the one who spreads the earth out flat

games.q: the week's Names — tap the pairs.
p: counts every hello, and is enough
vast in mercy and in knowledge

s: Al-Wasi' means vast in space and nothing more
2:115 joins it to knowing: All-Embracing, All-Knowing; 7:156 to mercy that embraces all things.
in 55:27, majesty comes paired with generous honor
al-Ghazali said the Nourisher feeds only bodies
bodies with food, and hearts with knowledge (Al-Muqit's day).

games.q: your little cousin asks why God would forgive someone who was mean to her. which line from this week fits best?
o: 'His mercy embraces all things, so there's room even for them.'
'God only forgives people who were nice in the first place.'
'God doesn't notice small mean things, so it doesn't matter.'
games.why: "My mercy embraceth all things" (7:156). and the second wrong answer forgets Ar-Raqib: every word is seen.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone you're up against right now, or someone hard to like. See them on an ordinary day: nervous, hoping, trying, the way you do.
Then let each breath go a little wider than the last, as if your chest were making room. If a sharp thought about them comes, let it pass, and widen again. Stay with them there until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Al-Wasi'. The All-Encompassing, vast in mercy and in knowledge. Name forty-five, and the week is done.

orig.note: Arabic: the All-Encompassing, the Vast. 2:115 pairs it with al-'Alim, the All-Knowing.

carryVoice: The week's last line: vast, wide enough for all things, so wide enough for one more. Week done.
